title: Creative-industry meeting at Old Naledi grounds over closure and livelihood
scope: One reported public meeting on 8 Dec. No counts from the separate GSS Grounds gathering are carried over.
organizer: Creative sector conveners; musician Vee Mampeezy named as convenor
demands: Reopen performing/creative industry following state COVID closure; engage government and Presidential Task Force; a Gazette account also reports a call for Culture Minister to step down.
demand_category: pending scientific review; possible social restrictions/policy response
participants_original: Government ministry statement says attendance exceeded the 50-person limit including young children; exact total and adult-only count unknown.
threshold_50_evidence: DailyNews quoting Ministry press release: attendance at Old Naledi public gathering on 8 Dec exceeded 50, including children. Exact total unknown; no other gatherings pooled.

state_response.accommodation: unknown; ministry reported ongoing stakeholder engagement and relief program, but whether this was a response to the gathering is unclear
state_response.arrests: unknown for the gathering; later Gazette report says Vee and other artists were charged, with Vee fined P10,000
state_response.crowd_dispersal: unknown for this Old Naledi gathering; police dispersal is reported for separate GSS gathering

scientific_verification: pending independent scientific review; writer has not verified provisional
episode_ownership: pending review: same creative-industry campaign also had a separate reported GSS Grounds gathering on 7 Dec; do not combine its crowd or state-action details.

start_date.summary: Gazette Dec 9 describes Tuesday's Old Naledi meeting; ministry DailyNews report explicitly dates meeting 8 Dec.

end_date.summary: One event date reported; no end time/next-day continuation of this gathering established.

location.summary: Both Gazette and Ministry account place the relevant meeting at Old Naledi grounds; Gaborone is stated in one article/page metadata.

demands.summary: Gazette reports a campaign to reopen creative industry and seek Presidential Task Force/MP intervention; one speaker calls for minister resignation.

participants_min.summary: Ministry press release states attendance exceeded the 50 limit, including young children; exact number unknown.

state_response.summary: Later Gazette reports charges/fine linked to open Old Naledi creatives meeting; Ministry statement records protocol violation and ongoing engagement. No same-day police dispersal at Old Naledi established.
